kashika: मुखसहिता नासिका मुखनासिका, तया च उच्चार्यते वर्णः सोऽनुनासिकसंज्ञो भवति। <<आङोऽनुनासिकश्छन्दसि>> [[६.१.१२६]] — अ॒भ्र आँ अ॒पः (ऋ० ५.४८.१)। ग॒भी॒र आँ उग्र॑पुत्रे (ऋ० ८.६७.११)। च न आँ इन्द्रः। मुखग्रहणं किम्? अनुस्वारस्यैव हि स्यात्। नासिकाग्रहणं किम्? कचटतपानां मा भूत्। अनुनासिकप्रदेशाः — <<आङोऽनुनासिकश्छन्दसि>> [[६.१.१२६]] इत्येवमादयः॥
kashikaEnglish: A sound pronounced through both mouth and nose is called anunāsika (nasalized).
englishShort: A letter whose pronunciation needs the usage of nose as well as mouth is called an अनुनासिक.
englishFull:
A sound pronounced through both the mouth and nose is called अनुनासिक (nasal).

The sūtra has: मुख "mouth," नासिका "nose," वचन "utterance," and अनुनासिकः "nasal."

**Anunāsika vowels:**
Any vowel can be nasalized: अँ, आँ, etc.

Vedic example: अभ्र आँ अपः (RV V.48.1)

**Anunāsika consonants:**
The five class-nasals are pronounced through both mouth and nose:
- ङ — throat + nose
- ञ — palate + nose
- ण — roof + nose
- न — teeth + nose
- म — lips + nose

Semivowels य, व, ल can also be nasalized.

**Why "mouth"?**
Excludes अनुस्वार, which is pronounced through the nose alone.

**Why "nose"?**
Excludes क, च, ट, त, प, etc., which are pronounced through the mouth alone.
